title: Progressive invocation reconciliation with confidence-based name resolution
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Problem: When model responses are streamed and include tool invocations (both OpenAI-style tools and legacy function objects), downstream consumers need a reliable, deterministic view of which external API/function was invoked. Current shims either do strict name matching (fragile) or heavy-handed manual mapping (costly). Streaming exacerbates the problem because partial tokens can include name fragments, arguments that arrive over multiple chunks, and conflicting candidates from resolver heuristics.

Goal: Implement a runtime "progressive reconciliation" layer that: (1) aggregates partial streaming tokens to build an invocation candidate, (2) computes a confidence score for name/signature match between OpenAI-style tools and Redwood legacy functions using a lightweight similarity model + heuristic rules, (3) emits a canonicalized invocation event once confidence crosses a threshold or at call completion, and (4) records telemetry and fallback traces when ambiguous mappings occur. The layer must be opt-in behind a feature flag and support a soft-fallback to existing exact-match behavior.
background: We already have a canonical-toolname registry (ENG-51830) plus several adapter shims that normalize signatures. However, most adapters expect full call payloads and do not handle streaming fragments or uncertainty gracefully. Customers reported mismatches when migrating from legacy functions to the OpenAI tools surface: logs show half-invocations, repeated retries, and missed metrics. The new approach should reduce noise in telemetry, improve success rates for automatic compatibility routing, and enable safer rollout of name migration bundles.
proposal:
1) Build a streaming buffer abstraction in the runtime that tags tokens with candidate recognition metadata (e.g., token offsets, partial JSON parse state).
2) Implement a small heuristic similarity scorer: exact name match, prefix/suffix match, normalized punctuation/tokenization match, and parameter-shape similarity (set of required keys matched roughly). Score components are weighted and combined into a single confidence float expressed as a string (for exports).
3) Expose an API: Runtime.emitInvocationCandidate({candidates: [...], confidence: "0.87", partial: true/false}) — but represented to Linear as guidance in docs.
4) On threshold pass, convert candidate to canonical key from registry and write a single InvocationResolved event to tracing and metrics. If no threshold reached on EOF, emit InvocationAmbiguous with top-N choices and include a recommended fallback policy.
5) Ship behind feature flag "progressive-invocation-reconcile" with a per-tenant opt-in for Dedicated/Private.
6) Add a console dashboard to surface ambiguous events per model/route so PMs can inspect and tune name mappings.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime accepts streaming tool/function tokens and reconstructs invocation bodies across at least 3 streaming fragmentation patterns (token split, mid-JSON, nested-string chunks).
Confidence scorer produces deterministic scores for seeded matching cases (unit tests stable).
InvocationResolved events include canonical key, input slice, confidence, and mapping rule used. InvocationAmbiguous events include top-3 candidates and diagnostic token offsets.

End-to-end integration test: migrate a legacy function to an OpenAI-style tool name; with feature on, >95% of test runs map correctly without manual mapping entries; with feature off, behavior remains unchanged.
Feature flag toggle documented and constrained to runtime-only mode for initial rollout; telemetry surfaces per-tenant ambiguous rate under the console release page.
Security review completed and signoff recorded for telemetry payloads (no secrets in events).
tasks: Spec: detailed scorer weights and tokenization rules (doc link)
Runtime: streaming buffer + partial JSON parser integration
Scoring: implement weighted similarity scorer and unit tests
Tracing/Telemetry: define InvocationResolved/InvocationAmbiguous schema and logging hooks
Feature flag: add progressive-invocation-reconcile with per-tenant opt-in
Console: dashboard mockup and metric wiring
E2E tests: migration scenario harness with legacy and new tool surfaces
Performance: benchmark latency overhead under 99th token path
implementation_notes: Keep the scorer implementation deterministic and platform-agnostic; avoid heavy ML models initially. Use tokenized normalized forms and a simple parameter-shape fingerprint (sorted required keys + approximate value types). The partial parser must be robust to streaming splits and maliciously crafted payloads (limit max buffer size and enforce parse timeouts).
testing_plan: Unit: scorer cases for exact/prefix/punctuation variations. Integration: streaming emulator that fragments payloads in randomized ways and asserts correct resolution or classified ambiguity. Load: run qps benchmark with feature enabled and compare p50/p95/p99 overhead to baseline; target <3% added p99 latency. Monitoring: increase alerting for ambiguous-rate >0.1% per-route after rollout.
rollout_plan: 1) Internal dogfood (redwood-internal) enablement for 1 week, collect ambiguous metrics. 2) Gradual opt-in for 5 Dedicated customers with high tool-calling volume. 3) If ambiguous rate stable and error rate not increased, enable default opt-in for newly created tenants and leave opt-out flag for older tenants. 4) Post-rollout: automated mapping suggestion job to propose registry entries based on observed high-confidence mappings.
risks_and_mitigations: False positives: mitigate with high initial threshold and conservative weight on fuzzy matches
Performance regression: micro-benchmark and gating; allow feature to be turned off per-tenant
Telemetry leakage: strip any sensitive values from logged invocation slices and enforce KMS access controls on logs
Operator confusion: add clear console indicators and an audit trail for automated mappings
